### webgpu/hdr-loader.js
Parses Radiance RGBE (.hdr) files. Supports new-style RLE scanlines.

Exports: loadHDR(url: string) → Promise<{ width, height, data: Float32Array }>
  Returns 4 floats per pixel (RGBA), suitable for rgba32float textures.

### webgpu/mip-generator.js
AMD Single Pass Downsampler for WebGPU. Generates a full mip chain in two
compute dispatches (box-filter average). WGSL shader is embedded at build time.

Exports: generateMips(device: GPUDevice, texture: GPUTexture, mipCount?: number) → void
  Texture must be rgba32float with COPY_DST usage. Mip 0 must be populated.
  mipCount defaults to texture.mipLevelCount.

### webgpu/env-prefilter.js
IBL environment map prefiltering with GGX importance sampling and Hammersley
sequence. Generates roughness-based mip chain where each level is convolved
with a GGX specular lobe. Use with split-sum approximation for PBR.

Exports: prefilterEnvMap(device: GPUDevice, texture: GPUTexture, numSamples?: number) → void
  Mip 0 = sharp (roughness 0), mip N = fully diffuse (roughness 1).
  numSamples defaults to 1024. Higher = better quality, slower.
  Sample with: textureSampleLevel(tex, sampler, uv, roughness * maxMip)

### webgpu/geometry.js
Procedural mesh generators. Each returns { positions: Float32Array,
normals: Float32Array, indices: Uint16Array }.

Exports: createCube(size?), createSphere(radius?, segments?),
  createCylinder(radiusTop?, radiusBottom?, height?, segments?),
  createPlane(width?, depth?),
  createBox(width?, height?, depth?),
  createTorus(radius?, tube?, radialSegments?, tubularSegments?)
  - createBox: axis-aligned box with independent full extents per axis
    (createCube is the uniform-size special case).
  - createTorus: ring in the XZ plane; radius = major, tube = minor radius;
    radialSegments subdivide the tube, tubularSegments the ring.

### webgpu/buffer.js
GPU buffer creation helper.

Exports: createBuffer(device: GPUDevice, data: ArrayBufferView, usage: GPUBufferUsageFlags) → GPUBuffer
  Creates a buffer pre-filled with data via mappedAtCreation.

### webgpu/context.js
WebGPU device + canvas context initialization.

Exports: initWebGPU(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, features?: GPUFeatureName[],
    options?: { powerPreference?: GPUPowerPreference, limits?: Record<string, number> })
  → Promise<{ device, ctx, format, adapter } | null>
  Returns null if WebGPU is unavailable. Features are only requested if
  the adapter supports them. options.powerPreference is passed to
  requestAdapter; options.limits raises device limits by name to
  min(adapter's supported value, your cap) (Infinity = adapter max; names the
  adapter doesn't report are skipped). The result includes the GPUAdapter
  (for adapter.info / limits / features).

### webgpu/sky.js
Equirectangular HDRI sky renderer. Fullscreen triangle, no vertex buffer.
Includes Reinhard tonemapping.

Exports:
  createSky(device, format, hdriView, hdriSampler, depthFormat?) → Sky
  drawSky(pass, sky) → void
  Write invViewProj to sky.uniformBuffer before calling drawSky.

### webgpu/shaders.js
Shader-source loading (backend-agnostic; works for WGSL or GLSL text). Typical
call site: const base = new URL('./shaders/', import.meta.url); then
loadShaders(base, ['a.wgsl', 'b.wgsl']).

Exports:
  loadShader(url: string | URL) → Promise<string>
    Fetches the URL as text; throws (with the URL) on a non-OK response.
  loadShaders(baseUrl: string | URL, names: string[]) → Promise<string[]>
    Resolves each name against baseUrl (pass a directory URL ending in '/');
    returns the sources in the same order as names.

### webgpu/canvas.js
Canvas backing-store sizing for HiDPI rendering (backend-agnostic).

Type: ResizeCanvasOptions = { maxDpr?: number; roundTo?: number }
Exports:
  resizeCanvasToDisplay(canvas, options?) → boolean
    Sets canvas.width/height from clientWidth/Height * min(maxDpr, devicePixelRatio)
    (maxDpr default 2, roundTo default 1). Returns true if the size changed, so
    callers reconfigure the swap chain / depth buffer only when needed.

### webgpu/camera.js
Orbit + first-person look cameras: spherical eye + drag-to-rotate + wheel-zoom,
and drag-to-look yaw/pitch. The math helpers are pure (no DOM);
createOrbitController / createLookController wire pointer (+ wheel) events onto
an element. Imports Vec3/Mat4 helpers from ../math.

Types: OrbitControllerOptions = { azimuth?, elevation?, distance?, target?,
  rotateSpeed?, minDistance?, maxDistance?, minElevation?, maxElevation?, zoomSpeed? };
  OrbitController = { azimuth, elevation, distance, target, eye(): Vec3,
  viewMatrix(up?: Vec3): Mat4, dispose(): void };
  LookState = { azDeg, elDeg } (degrees; azDeg wrapped to (-180, 180], 0 = +Z);
  LookDragOptions = { sensDegPerPx? = 0.25, invertY?, minElDeg? = -89, maxElDeg? = 89 };
  LookControllerOptions = LookDragOptions + { azDeg?, elDeg?, onChange?(state) };
  LookController = { azDeg, elDeg, dir(): Vec3, viewMatrix(eye, up?): Mat4,
  dispose(): void }.
Exports:
  orbitEye(target, azimuth, elevation, distance) → Vec3
    target + distance * [cosEl*sinAz, sinEl, cosEl*cosAz].
  dirFromAzEl(azimuth, elevation) → Vec3
    unit direction [cosEl*sinAz, sinEl, cosEl*cosAz] (e.g. a sun/light vector).
  createOrbitController(canvas, options?) → OrbitController
    Drag updates azimuth/elevation (clamped); the wheel scales distance
    exponentially (clamped), normalising deltaMode line/page units to pixels.
  applyLookDrag(state, dxPx, dyPx, opts?) → LookState
    Pure look-drag step, owning THE sign convention: pointer right = look right
    (azDeg -= dx*sens), pointer up = look up (invertY flips); elevation clamped,
    azimuth wrapped; returns a new state. dirFromAzEl(azDeg*PI/180, elDeg*PI/180)
    is the matching view direction.
  createLookController(element, options?) → LookController
    Pointer-drag first-person look at a fixed eye, feeding applyLookDrag (same
    convention); live azDeg/elDeg, dir()/viewMatrix(eye, up?) per frame,
    onChange(state) per drag update.

### webgpu/scan.js
GPU exclusive prefix scan (Blelloch, 512 elements/block, recursive levels —
3 levels cover 134M elements) over a u32 region of a storage buffer. The
input, output, and scratch regions live in ONE buffer at arbitrary ELEMENT
offsets (bases travel in a uniform, so no 256-byte bind-offset alignment and
no second writable binding — fused buffer layouts just work). planScan is
pure (unit-tested); createScan/prepare/encode are GPU-bound. Workgroups are
256 threads (WebGPU default limits suffice); dispatches auto-split into 2D
grids when a level exceeds maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension. The pure level
math lives in webgpu/scan-plan.js (no shader import — loads under node) and
is re-exported by scan.js, so consumers import scan.js alone.

Types: ScanDispatch = { x, y };
  ScanLevelPlan = { count, blocks, sumsBase, scanDispatch, addbackDispatch };
  ScanPlan = { count, levels: ScanLevelPlan[], scratchElems, grandTotalElem };
  ScanRegion = { buffer: GPUBuffer, count, srcElem, dstElem, scratchElem };
  PreparedScan = { plan, grandTotalElem, encode(pass), destroy() };
  GpuScan = { prepare(region): PreparedScan }.
Exports:
  SCAN_BLOCK_SIZE = 512, SCAN_ADDBACK_SIZE = 256
  planScan(count, maxWorkgroupsPerDim? = 65535) → ScanPlan
    PURE level math: level 0 scans src→dst, each next level scans the previous
    level's block sums in place inside scratch until one block remains; the
    LAST level's sums[0] is the grand total (sum of all inputs, written even
    for count 0). scratchElems = u32 elements the caller must reserve;
    grandTotalElem is scratch-relative.
  createScan(device) → GpuScan
    Compiles the two pipelines once per device.
  GpuScan.prepare({ buffer, count, srcElem, dstElem, scratchElem }) → PreparedScan
    Bakes one region layout into per-level uniforms + bind groups (create
    once; re-prepare only when buffer/count/bases change; destroy() the old
    one). dstElem may equal srcElem (in-place). buffer needs STORAGE usage
    and is bound whole (must fit maxStorageBufferBindingSize).
  PreparedScan.encode(pass: GPUComputePassEncoder) → void
    Records the dispatches into a CALLER-owned compute pass (wrap it in your
    own timestamp window, keep issuing dependent dispatches in the same
    pass); zero per-frame allocation. Afterwards dst[i] = sum of src[0..i)
    and the grand total sits at the ABSOLUTE element PreparedScan.grandTotalElem
    (copyBufferToBuffer it out if needed). Resets pipeline/bind group 0 —
    restore yours after.

### webgpu/fly-camera.js
First-person fly ("noclip") camera building on webgpu/camera.js: applyLookDrag
supplies the look half (pointer-up = look-up), this adds WASD-style key
flight, wheel dolly, and two-finger pinch dolly. flyMoveDelta/dollyDelta are
pure (unit-tested); createFlyController is DOM-bound. Backend-agnostic
(WebGL or WebGPU — it only produces positions/matrices).

Types: FlyMoveState = { forward, back, left, right, up, down: boolean };
  FlyControllerOptions = LookDragOptions + { position?, azDeg?, elDeg?,
  moveSpeed? = 5 (units/s), wheelSpeed? = 0.01 (units per normalized wheel px),
  pinchSpeed? = 0.08 (units per pinch px), up? = [0,1,0],
  keyMap? (KeyboardEvent.code → FlyMoveState key; default WASD + Space/E up, Q down),
  dragButtons? = [0, 2] };
  FlyController = { position, azDeg, elDeg, dir(): Vec3, update(dt): void,
  viewMatrix(): Mat4, dispose(): void }.
Exports:
  flyMoveDelta(look, move, distance, up? = [0,1,0]) → Vec3
    Pure displacement for one movement step: forward/back along the full 3D
    view dir, left/right along normalize(cross(dir, up)), up/down along the
    world up axis; opposite keys cancel, diagonals sum (not renormalized).
  dollyDelta(look, amount) → Vec3
    Pure dolly along the view direction (positive = toward the view).
  createFlyController(element, options?) → FlyController
    Drag-to-look via applyLookDrag (buttons filtered by dragButtons; suppresses
    contextmenu when right-drag is enabled), key events on the element's
    document, wheel dolly (deltaMode-normalized, wheel-up dollies in), pinch
    dolly; call update(dt) once per frame to apply held keys. Held keys are
    cleared on window blur so an alt-tab mid-flight can't leave the camera
    drifting.
